segments.text: Imagine walking in to a massive jungle research lab.
You want to translate a text, but instead of one giant smart monkey,
you find a team of 896 specialized monkey scientists.
That is exactly how Kimi K3 works.
It is a massive mixture of experts model.
But does it actually beat Ali Baba's brand new QN3.8 Max?
Let us break down these two brand new Chinese AI giants
in under 3 minutes.
First, let us look at their size.
Kimi K3 is an absolute monster with 2.8 trillion parameters.
QN3.8 Max is slightly smaller coming in at 2.4 trillion.
But wait, why does size matter?
More parameters mean the model can store more knowledge and spot deeper patterns.
However, running a model this big is incredibly expensive.
How do they keep it fast and cheap?
They use a trick called mixture of experts or MOE.
Think of it like this.
When you ask Kimi K3 a question, it does not wake up all 896 scientists.
It only activates the 16 best monkeys for your specific question.
That keeps it fast and energy efficient.
Plus, moonshot AI introduced two secret weapons called Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals.
These tricks make Kimi K3 2.5 times more efficient at moving information than before.
Isn't that a massive leap?
What about Ali Baba's QN3.8 Max?
Ali Baba hasn't shared its exact expert count.
But they claim it's a multimodal beast that handles text, images, video and documents easily.
In early testing, Ali Baba ranks its second only to clawed 5 Fable.
Both models have a massive 1 million token context window.
That's like handing them a thousand-page book to read in one second.
But Kimi K3 has an insane pricing advantage.
If you ask it a question about a document it already read, it retrieves pre-peeled bananas from its cash.
This cash hit gets you a 90% discount, costing just 30 cents per million tokens.
For new questions, it costs $3.
QN3.8 Max is currently in preview, offering monthly subscription plans instead.
So, which model wins the crown?
If you need long horizon coding or deep repository search, Kimi K3 is your champion.
If you need a multimodal agent to handle video and images, QN3.8 Max takes the lead.
Both models are changing the game.
Which one will you try first?
